module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 828

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/828](https://www.erdosproblems.com/828)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos828

open scoped Nat

/--
Is it true that, for any $a \in \mathbb{Z}$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that
$$\phi(n) | n + a$$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_828 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ a : ℤ, Set.Infinite {n : ℕ | ↑(φ n) ∣ n + a} := by
  sorry

/--
When $n > 1$, Lehmer conjectured that $\phi(n) | n - 1$ if and only if $n$ is prime.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_828.variants.lehmer_conjecture : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n > 1, φ n ∣ n - 1 ↔ Prime n := by
  sorry

/--
It is an easy exercise to show that $\phi(n) | n$ if and only if $n = 0, 1$ or $n = 2^a 3^b$ for
some $a > 0$.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
"https://github.com/XC0R/formal-conjectures/blob/03e00cf8d44098d0fb06e891fca30c29769df619/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/828.lean#L49"]
theorem erdos_828.variants.phi_dvd_self_iff_pow2_pow3 {n : ℕ} :
    φ n ∣ n ↔ n ≤ 1 ∨ ∃ᵉ (a > 0) (b), n = 2 ^ a * 3 ^ b := by
  sorry

end Erdos828

reformulations.difference: The solution set ranges over all natural numbers, including zero, rather than only positive integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every fixed integer a, imposing n > 0 removes at most the singleton {0}. Removing a finite set preserves infinitude. The pointwise equivalence was proved in scratch.lean as review_infinite_iff_positive; universal quantification over a preserves it.

reformulations.difference: Compared with the corrected positive-integer classification in the source discussion, Lean additionally includes n = 0 and writes the exceptional cases as n ≤ 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The discussion corrects the classification to n = 1 or n = 2^a * 3^b with a ≥ 1 and b ≥ 0. On positive naturals, n ≤ 1 is equivalent to n = 1. The added zero case is true because Nat.totient 0 = 0 and 0 divides 0. The equivalence of the universally quantified classifications was proved as review_classification_iff_positive without using the admitted problem theorem.

review.notes: All three mathematical statements were checked. The website's main prose incorrectly permits a = 0, b > 0 in its ancillary classification; its discussion explicitly corrects this, and Lean follows the correction. The counterexample n = 3 to the uncorrected prose was verified in Lean. Integer coercions, the Lehmer variant's bounded natural subtraction, generic Prime versus Nat.Prime, and extended existential binders were checked. Small computations agreed with the classification through n = 100 and found no composite Lehmer solutions through n = 200. Scratch equivalence proofs compiled without sorryAx. The reviewed file was not modified.
